core_prompt: What evidence matters for my reading goal?

card_hints.observation: 1 sentence on what the data shows — BEFORE reading what the authors claim. Then panel-by-panel notes if needed.
card_hints.question: Parking a question? Write it here. Resolve it in Pass 3 without overwriting your interpretation.
card_hints.audit: Graph audit: axes + labels / units / scale (lin vs log) / n / error bars named (SD, SEM or 95% CI) / significant or error-prone? One line per key panel.

fields.label: Pipeline sketch
fields.hint: 3-5 boxes, input (cells, animals, initial mesh) → output (assay readout, simulation metric). Boxes only; arrows carry the logic.

fields.label: Parking lot note
fields.hint: Unfamiliar terms/techniques go in the Parking lot list below — don't stop to Google mid-pass.

checklist: Can I explain the main claim without looking at the paper?
Can I summarise the main thrust WITH its supporting evidence?
Did I verify sample size (n) and error-bar definition for key results?
Do I have 2-5 unread references queued for background?
todos: Figures, diagrams, illustrations BEFORE the results text — one sentence of what the data shows, before their claim
Audit every key graph (labels, units, scale, n, error bars, significance)
Park unfamiliar terms/equations instead of Googling mid-pass
Mark unread references worth coming back to
note: Fine not to understand everything: (1) unfamiliar terminology/acronyms, (2) hard proofs or technique, (3) poor writing. Park it, read background, then either come back or push on to Pass 3.
